nodes.label: Wireframes Draft 2 (revised scope)
nodes.rationale: Fourteen screens across three surfaces. Draft 1's points ledger, tiers, earn rates, segment/targeting engine, tenant isolation, POS integration and WhatsApp campaign layer were all removed after the client confirmed a single-property programme with a fixed schedule.

nodes.label: Member App Screens (01)
nodes.rationale: Claim membership, verify consent, Explore, Offers, Benefit detail, Search, Digital card, Profile. Everything visible without tapping, because the paper sheet showed all five categories at once and hiding terms would be a downgrade.

nodes.label: Staff Verification Page (02)
nodes.rationale: A web page, not a fourth product — opened on whatever device is already at the counter, so no installation or procurement. Staff sign in individually so every redemption is attributed to a named person. The system records; it does not discount.

nodes.label: Admin Dashboard Wireframes (03)
nodes.rationale: Members, member detail, reporting and benefit management — the 'backend access' the client described. Small by design: a list of dozens, not thousands, so a simple table beats an analytics product.

nodes.label: Rotating Digital Card Code
nodes.rationale: Draft 2 specified an opaque, automatically refreshing payload: these are high-value benefits, so a static code that could be screenshotted and forwarded would be worth real money, and a stale payload fails verification. The code identifies but does not authorise. Superseded in Version 3.

nodes.label: Tap-to-Call Reservations
nodes.rationale: Described as the highest-value small addition in the build: three benefits require phoning three different numbers currently printed on a sheet that gets lost. Nearly free to implement and it removes genuine friction. On desktop the number is displayed rather than dialled.

nodes.label: Benefit Management as the Test of Delivery
nodes.rationale: Changing the F&B discount from 25% to 20% must be a form field. If it needs a developer and a release, the client does not have backend access regardless of how good the rest looks. Discounts, caps, phone numbers and terms are all configuration read at runtime.

nodes.label: No Member List or Name Search for Staff
nodes.rationale: Staff can retrieve only the person in front of them, by exact number or scan. Given who these members are, that restriction is the point rather than a detail.

nodes.label: Masked Contact Details and Visible Access Notice
nodes.rationale: Phone and email are masked by default so revealing one is a deliberate, logged action. Telling staff on the screen itself that their viewing is logged is a stronger control than the log alone.

nodes.label: Per-Channel Consent, Unticked by Default
nodes.rationale: Qatar's data protection law requires explicit prior consent specifically for direct electronic marketing, so bundling it into activation would invalidate it. The printed sheet already promises notification by the member's preferred channel, making it a programme commitment rather than only a marketing preference.

nodes.label: Responsive Strategy
nodes.rationale: Member experience mobile-first widening at ~900px (tab bar becomes top nav, lists go one to three columns, list-and-detail split); admin desktop-first collapsing below it; verification page equal at both sizes. Desktop is not a wider phone and earns its place by reducing navigation, not expanding scope.

nodes.label: Arabic / Right-to-Left Planning
nodes.rationale: RTL affects sidebar position, table column order and text alignment on every screen, so it must be planned from the start rather than retrofitted.
